doc.title: Hubert Laws — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The Met orchestra and joining CTI
title: Being the only black player at the Met
summary: Laws realizes he was the only black musician in the Met and notes how few black players remain in orchestras.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Were there any other black performers when you were in the Met?

Not in the Met. As a matter of fact, I was so naive. I used to walk around there wondering why everybody knew my name. That’s how stupid I was. No, I said, I got to learn these guys’ names. They all know my name. Hey man, you’re the only black one walking around here. That’s what occurred to me later. Isn’t that something? Even now, it hasn’t changed that much in these orchestras, just a few. What’s – Watt, he just retired from the L.A. Phil. He played french horn. I went to his retirement party. There aren’t too many blacks. There are maybe two or three in the L. A. Phil. It’s pretty much the same thing all over. But what can you do? I tell anybody who plays an instrument, learn to improvise too. Learn to improvise. Why should you limit yourself? Do all that stuff, and you increase your bargaining power.
